readings.abstract: This bundle ships the network the campaign selected, under a verdict that did not go its way: on the held-out part a logistic regression on the same shaped features scored better, by a margin whose interval clears zero. It ships because the downstream dispatcher needs a calibrated score and the linear baseline does not produce one — that is the recorded stance, and it is the whole reason this bundle exists rather than a one-line scikit-learn call. What it reproduces is exact: every held-out row, from raw input through the shaper's own fitted transform and the selected checkpoint, to the scores the evaluation stored. What it must not be taken for is a better ranker than the baseline it lost to.
readings.intended_use:
Use this model to score an order for the risk that it arrives late, at the moment the order is placed and from the fields a caller already holds. It expects one row per order, in the input schema this page lists, and it answers one row per row given — it never drops or reorders, so a caller may join the result back by position.

Do not use it to rank orders against a baseline it did not beat. The evaluation found a linear model better on the held-out part, and the reason this network ships anyway is the calibrated score it produces, not its ranking. If your use is ranking alone, take the baseline.

Do not use it far outside the ranges the training data covered. The schema table on this page carries the range seen for every numeric column and the vocabulary seen for every categorical one; a value beyond them is answered and flagged in the row's warnings, but the answer is extrapolation and nothing measured it. An unseen category is a defined state, not an error: it lands on the reserved code the shaper set aside for exactly that, and the row says so.

Do not use it where the distances are short. The evaluation split the part at the median distance and found the model working on the far half and not on the near one; the near half is where its answers should be treated as uninformative rather than merely uncertain. That finding is on this page and in the model card, with its row counts.

And do not treat a score as a probability. It is the network's raw output, which for this head is a logit; the page says how to read it as one, and the decision threshold the evaluation chose on the valid part is recorded beside it.
